issues.title: Activating "Clear filters" removes the focused button and drops keyboard focus to the document body

priority.rationale: Components index is a primary navigation workflow (section landing page) and the same DirectoryFilters plus EmptyState pairing is reused in the Resource directory pattern, so one shared fix reaches every instance. Every keyboard and screen-reader user who filters hits it. Low effort, no product dependency.

affectedUsers: Blind and low-vision screen-reader users (focus position lost; virtual cursor may reset)
Sighted keyboard-only users (no visible focus indicator after activation)
Screen-magnifier users (magnifier loses the focus point)
Switch and voice-control users who rely on focus position

locations.component: EmptyState action and DirectoryFilters summary button

issues.pattern: Filter reset command (button) inside a search landmark and as the empty-state recovery action. See pattern matrix row P-08 'Directory filters and result count' and P-10 'Empty state'.
issues.observedBehavior: After Enter on either Clear filters button, the button is unmounted (filters return to default, hasActiveFilters is false and the empty state disappears) and document.activeElement is <body>. No focus indicator is visible anywhere. In Edge the next Tab reaches the first result link ('Box') and Shift+Tab reaches the Maturity select, because the browser keeps a sequential-navigation starting point. Reproduced on all 4 combinations tested (summary/empty-state button x Tab/Shift+Tab) and in the directory demo.
issues.expectedBehavior: After filters are cleared, focus is placed on a logical, visible, still-present element, for example the Search input or the result-count status/results heading. The cleared state stays announced through the existing role=status count ('Showing 29 of 29').
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155 at 1280x900, fresh profile, open http://localhost:5173/components?q=zzzz.
Press Tab until 'Clear filters' (either the one beside 'Showing 0 of 29' or the one in the 'No components match these filters' empty state) is focused; observe the focus ring.
Press Enter.
Observe: the list returns to 29 items, the button disappears, no focus ring is visible; in DevTools document.activeElement is <body>.
Repeat on /patterns/resource-directory with Demo scenario 'No results' and the empty-state 'Clear filters' button.

evidence.method: Playwright keyboard focus + Enter, then read document.activeElement; then Tab / Shift+Tab
evidence.observation: focusAfterActivate 'BODY' for both buttons; next Tab 'a "Box" in main'; Shift+Tab 'select "Any maturity…" in main'.

evidence.method: Same, including directory No results scenario
evidence.observation: directoryNoResults.focusAfterActivate 'body'.
{"el":"body"}

issues.bestPracticeRationale: Losing focus to the body forces keyboard and screen-reader users to re-find their place and removes the visible focus indicator. It is not recorded as a 2.4.3 Focus Order failure because Edge kept a sequential-navigation starting point and the next Tab and Shift+Tab destinations were logical (evidence/focus-loss.json), so the order itself was not impeded in the tested browser. Screen-reader behaviour after focus loss (some reset the virtual cursor to the top of the document) could not be tested (BLK-001). APG guidance that focus moves to a logical element when the invoking element no longer exists supports the expected behaviour.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.3 Focus Order
sources.relevantGuidance: Failure only when focus order impedes meaning or operation; 'focus returns to the button or the element following the button' example for dialogs.
sources.caveats: Does not explicitly address focus lost to body; used to justify the best-practice classification.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A)
sources.relevantGuidance: Focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
sources.caveats: Opened to decide applicability; not cited as failed.

sources.title: ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) Pattern
sources.relevantGuidance: Note 2: when the invoking element no longer exists, focus is set on another element that provides logical work flow.
sources.caveats: Dialog-specific guidance applied by analogy to a self-removing control.

sources.title: ARIA APG Developing a Keyboard Interface
sources.relevantGuidance: Discernible and predictable keyboard focus: users need to discover where focus landed after a key press.
sources.caveats: Section is marked as work in progress (APG issue 217).

sourceRequirements.requirement: When the element that had focus is removed, place focus on another element that continues the workflow.
Focus location must remain discernible after a keyboard action.

engineeringJudgment: Search input is the most useful target: the user cleared filters to start a new search, and the role=status count already reports the result. Moving focus to the status text instead would need tabIndex=-1 on a live region, which some AT announce twice.

Both buttons call the same onChange(defaultFilters) path; DirectoryFilters can own the handoff for its own button, and the two EmptyState call sites need the same behaviour, so a small shared helper (for example a ref to the search input exposed by DirectoryFilters or a 'clear' callback that focuses it) avoids duplicate code.
Severity medium (not high): a logical next Tab destination exists in Edge, and the action is non-destructive.
issues.likelyRootCause: DirectoryFilters renders Clear filters only while hasActiveFilters(filters) (DirectoryFilters.tsx:106), and EmptyState renders its action only while results.length === 0 (ComponentsIndexPage.tsx:38-41, ResourceDirectory.tsx:171-175). Activation makes the condition false and React unmounts the focused button; no code moves focus first.
issues.proposedFix: Give DirectoryFilters a ref to its Search input (forwarded from Field/Input) and a clear handler that calls onChange(defaultFilters) and then focuses the Search input after render (requestAnimationFrame or a layout effect keyed on the clear). Expose that handler (or the ref) so ComponentsIndexPage and ResourceDirectory empty-state 'Clear filters' buttons use the same path. Keep the role=status count unchanged so the new count is still announced. Do not keep the button mounted as a disabled control (that would leave an inert stop in the tab order).
issues.risksAndDependencies: Touches the shared DirectoryFilters (Components index with URL state, directory demo with local state). Focusing the input must not trigger the 'query changes do not move focus' route logic in usePageTitle; the URL change from ?q=… to no query is a query-only change and should keep the input focus. Existing e2e tests in e2e/patterns.spec.ts and e2e/accessibility.spec.ts may assert on the current state.
acceptanceCriteria: On /components?q=zzzz, activating either Clear filters with Enter or Space leaves document.activeElement on a visible, connected element inside main (expected: the Search input), with a visible focus outline (computed outline-style not 'none').
Same on /patterns/resource-directory for the summary button and the No results empty-state button.
After activation the role=status count text reads 'Showing 29 of 29' (Components) / 'Showing 12 of 48 entries' (directory), unchanged in wording.
document.activeElement is never <body> after activating any 'Clear filters' button (automated check).
manualVerification: Edge, keyboard only, 1280x900: open /components?q=zzzz, Tab to the summary Clear filters, press Enter; confirm the visible focus ring is on the Search input and the input is empty.
Reload, Tab to the empty-state Clear filters, press Space; same expectation.
On /patterns/resource-directory choose Demo scenario 'No results', activate Clear filters in the empty state; same expectation.
Repeat at 320x640 to confirm the focused input is scrolled into view.
If a screen reader becomes available (BLK-001): confirm the input is announced and the count status is spoken.
issues.candidateAutomatedTest: Playwright e2e in e2e/patterns.spec.ts (or accessibility.spec.ts): goto /components?q=zzzz, focus each Clear filters button, press Enter, expect(page.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Search' })).toBeFocused(). A Vitest + Testing Library test on DirectoryFilters with a stateful wrapper can assert toHaveFocus() after userEvent.click. Limits: does not cover AT announcement.

remediation.notes: Shared fix in the owning feature: DirectoryFilters forwards a ref to its Search input, and its own Clear filters button focuses that input before calling onChange(defaultFilters), so focus moves before the button unmounts. New exported hook useClearDirectoryFilters(onChange) returns { searchRef, clear }; ComponentsIndexPage and ResourceDirectory pass searchRef to DirectoryFilters and use clear for their EmptyState Clear filters buttons. The role=status count is unchanged. The URL change from ?q= to none is query-only, so usePageTitle leaves focus on the input. Not run: 320x640 scroll-into-view check; screen reader (BLK-001).

issues.title: Completion of a demo load is not announced when it ends in an empty result or in the resource detail view

priority.rationale: Async status feedback is a core teaching point of the three pattern pages and appears in five scenario outcomes. Screen-reader users hear 'Loading…' and then nothing. One shared approach (a persistent status region per demo) fixes all instances; no product decision needed.

affectedUsers: Users of AT that surfaces status messages for cognitive support
issues.pattern: Async request status (loading, success, empty, error) in pattern demos. See pattern matrix row P-11 'Scenario loading / empty / error / retry'.
issues.observedBehavior: Each demo mounts <Text role="status">Loading …</Text> while pending and unmounts it on completion. Success in the directory and dashboard announces through the DirectoryFilters/Dashboard count status ('Showing 12 of 48 entries', 'Showing 23 of 23 changes'), and errors through role="alert". But: Directory 'Empty' and Dashboard 'Empty' add only an EmptyState heading and paragraph with no live region (MutationObserver log: only 'ADDED status: Loading entries…'). Resource detail 'Success' and 'Empty' insert only an empty role=status ('ADDED status: ') and replace the heading text. Focus stays on the Demo scenario select (or body), so nothing tells a non-sighted user that loading finished or what the result was.
issues.expectedBehavior: When a demo request finishes, a status message that is programmatically exposed (role=status / polite live region that persists across states) states the outcome, for example 'No entries yet.', 'No activity yet.', 'Button entry loaded.', 'Button entry loaded. No recorded changes.', without moving focus.
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155, 1280x900, open http://localhost:5173/patterns/resource-directory and wait for the list.
In DevTools, observe live regions (or run the MutationObserver in evidence/scripts/interactions.mjs section 8).
With the keyboard, focus 'Demo scenario' and choose 'Empty' (Alt+Down, arrows, Enter).
Observe: 'Loading entries…' status appears then is removed; 'No entries yet' heading appears with no role=status/alert/aria-live ancestor and no live-region text change.
Repeat on /patterns/activity-dashboard (Empty) and /patterns/resource-detail (Success, then Empty).

evidence.method: MutationObserver recording live-region insertions and text changes during scenario changes
evidence.observation: directory empty: ['ADDED status: Loading entries…'] only; dashboard empty: ['ADDED status: Loading activity…'] only; resource-detail success: ['ADDED status: '] and empty: ['ADDED status: Loading the Button entry…','ADDED status: '].

evidence.method: Playwright ariaSnapshot of the demo section after the Empty scenario settles
evidence.observation: liveInSection [] and emptyAncestorsLive false for both directory and dashboard; snapshot shows region > heading 'No entries yet' [level=4] > paragraph > link.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.relevantGuidance: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties so AT can present them without focus.

sources.title: Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.relevantGuidance: Status message definition includes results of an action and waiting state; 'Removal of status text' section: when a busy/waiting message disappears, non-sighted users are unaware unless an equivalent status such as 'system available' is provided.
sources.caveats: Search result lists themselves are not status messages; the outcome summary is.

sources.title: MDN ARIA: status role
sources.relevantGuidance: status is a polite live region; do not move focus to it when it updates.
sources.caveats: AT support for regions inserted already populated varies (see LEAD-001).

sourceRequirements.requirement: The outcome of the load (result of an action) must be exposed through role or properties without receiving focus.
When a waiting message is removed, provide an equivalent status that the wait has ended.

engineeringJudgment: Prefer one persistent role=status element rendered for the life of each demo (outside the aria-busy section if LEAD-002 is confirmed) whose text changes per state; this also addresses LEAD-001 (populated insertion).
Success states that already announce a count can keep that count; avoid double announcements by keeping the outcome text brief or empty when the count status speaks.
Resource detail success could announce '<name> entry loaded.'; the focus move after Retry stays as is.
issues.likelyRootCause: The loading status is a conditionally mounted live region inside each demo (ResourceDirectory.tsx:109, ActivityDashboard.tsx:50, ResourceDetail.tsx:45). It is removed on completion, and only some outcome branches render their own status (DirectoryFilters count, Dashboard count, role=alert). EmptyState (src/design-system/composites/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx) is static by design and the empty/detail branches add no status.
issues.proposedFix: In each demo, render one persistent <Text role="status"> (or a small shared useRequest-aware StatusMessage in features/scenarios) that is present in every state, with text derived from state: pending → 'Loading entries…'; success with data → '' (count status speaks) or a short 'Entries loaded.'; success empty → 'No entries yet.'; error → '' (role=alert speaks). Resource detail: success → 'Button entry loaded.' (plus 'No recorded changes.' for the empty history). Keep EmptyState static. Keep skeletons aria-hidden.
issues.risksAndDependencies: Must not produce duplicate announcements with the existing count status and alerts. Verification of actual speech depends on BLK-001; DOM-level verification is possible.
acceptanceCriteria: For each of: directory Empty, dashboard Empty, detail Success, detail Empty, a single element with role=status (or aria-live=polite) that existed before the scenario change has its text changed to a non-empty outcome message after loading completes.
No outcome produces an empty-text status insertion as its only change.
Focus does not move as a result of loading completion (stays on the Demo scenario select).
Existing success counts and error alerts still appear exactly once.
manualVerification: Edge, keyboard only: on each pattern page, operate Demo scenario through every option; after each settles, inspect the persistent status element text in DevTools Accessibility pane.
Run evidence/scripts/interactions.mjs section 8 and confirm each state logs a 'TEXT' change on a persistent status with outcome wording.
If BLK-001 is resolved: NVDA + Edge, confirm 'No entries yet', 'No activity yet' and 'Button entry loaded' are spoken without focus moving.
issues.candidateAutomatedTest: Vitest + Testing Library in src/features/scenarios/scenarios.test.tsx or a pattern test: render ResourceDirectory with scenario 'empty', await findByRole('status') to have text 'No entries yet.' and assert the same status node persisted from the loading state. Playwright e2e for each page asserting getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: … }). Limits: cannot assert speech.

remediation.notes: Persistent status owned by ScenarioDemo (features/scenarios), because ScenarioDemo remounts the demo on every scenario change and reset, so a status inside the demo could not persist. ScenarioDemo renders one VisuallyHidden role=status after the stage (outside the keyed demo and outside the aria-busy section, which also addresses LEAD-002's risk) and provides a setter through context; new hook useScenarioStatus(message). Demos report: directory 'Loading entries…' / 'No entries yet.' / '' (count status or alert speaks); dashboard 'Loading activity…' / 'No activity yet.' / ''; detail 'Loading the Button entry…' / 'Button entry loaded.' plus ' No recorded changes.' when history is empty / '' on error. The visible loading text keeps its wording but no longer has role=status, to avoid a duplicate announcement. Success counts and alerts unchanged. Focus is not moved. Baseline before any change (same session): npm run lint exit 1 with 206 errors, all in untracked docs/accessibility/evidence/scripts/*.mjs (audit probe scripts using browser globals under the Node eslint config); npm run typecheck exit 0; npm test 31 files / 901 tests passed; e2e baseline run aborted environmentally (trace ENOENT, then ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on :4173) with 125 passed / 32 failed, none related to assertions.
testsAdded: src/features/scenarios/scenarios.test.tsx 'announces each demo state through one status message that persists across scenario changes (A11Y-002)' (same status node before/after scenario change and Reset, text 'No entries yet.', select keeps focus)

issues.title: Required confirmation checkbox in the proposal form is not identified as required

priority.rationale: Quick win in the only multi-field form. The submit-time error and summary recover it, so impact is limited, but the inconsistency with four fields marked '(required)' misleads users before they submit.

affectedUsers: Users with cognitive, language and learning disabilities
All users relying on the visible '(required)' convention
issues.pattern: Form field with required state and submit-time validation. See pattern matrix rows P-06 'Field' and P-07 'Form validation with error summary'.
issues.observedBehavior: Labels for the other four fields read 'Component name (required)', 'Component layer (required)', 'Summary (required)', 'Contact email (required)' and their controls have required=true. The checkbox label reads 'I searched the directory and nothing existing fits' with no visible required marker, required=false and no aria-required, yet validateProposal rejects an unchecked box ('Confirm that you searched the directory first.'). The requirement becomes known only after a failed submit.
issues.expectedBehavior: The checkbox shows the same '(required)' cue as the other fields (or the form states that all fields are required) and exposes the required state programmatically (required attribute or aria-required="true").
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155, 1280x900, open http://localhost:5173/patterns/form-validation.
Read the five field labels; note four show '(required)' and the checkbox does not.
Inspect the checkbox in DevTools Accessibility pane: Required is false.
Press Tab to 'Submit proposal' and press Enter with the checkbox unchecked.
Observe the error 'Confirm that you searched the directory first.' for the checkbox.

evidence.method: DOM inspection before and after submit
evidence.observation: before: required false, ariaRequired null; otherLabels show '(required)' on the four other fields only; after submit: aria-invalid true and error description associated.
['text:true','select-one:true','text:true','email:true','checkbox:false']
Checkbox with no required marker and the error text below.

evidence.method: Screenshot of the whole form after submit
evidence.observation: Four labels with '(required)', the checkbox without.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
sources.relevantGuidance: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

sources.title: Understanding SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
sources.relevantGuidance: Benefits: providing labels and instructions, including identification of required fields, prevents incomplete submissions. Techniques H90 (indicating required form controls using label or legend) and G83.
sources.caveats: Programmatic exposure of required state is better covered by 1.3.1 / 4.1.2; the primary failure recorded is the missing visible instruction given the form's own convention.

sources.title: Understanding SC 3.3.1 Error Identification
sources.relevantGuidance: Required-but-omitted input is an input error; programmatic required information may be covered by 4.1.2.
sources.caveats: 3.3.1 itself passes: the error is identified and described in text.

sourceRequirements.requirement: Identify required inputs in the label or instructions before submission.

engineeringJudgment: Field already renders a visual '(required)' (aria-hidden) plus the native required attribute; Checkbox lacks an equivalent prop, so the fix belongs in the Checkbox primitive (optional `required` cue) or at the call site.
Native required on a checkbox inside a noValidate form exposes 'required' to AT without triggering browser validation bubbles.

issues.title: After Retry the focused button disappears and focus sits on the body until loading succeeds

priority.rationale: Same three pattern demos as A11Y-002 and fixable in the same change. Focus is restored to the heading after ~1.5 s, so the window is short, but a Tab pressed in that window skips past the demo.

issues.pattern: Recovery action inside an error alert for an async request. See pattern matrix row P-11.
issues.observedBehavior: Pressing Enter on Retry sets state to pending, which unmounts the Alert and its Retry button; 150 ms later document.activeElement is <body>. Tab during loading moves to the region after the demo ('What each demo scenario renders'), Shift+Tab to 'Reset demo' (or the 'Directory' link on resource detail). When loading succeeds (about 1.5-3 s) focus is moved to the demo heading, as documented.
issues.expectedBehavior: Focus is never left on the body during the retry: it is moved immediately to a stable element (for example the demo heading, which already has tabIndex=-1) when Retry is activated, and remains there through success or a repeat error.
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155, 1280x900, open http://localhost:5173/patterns/resource-directory.
Choose Demo scenario 'Error' and wait for 'Entries could not be loaded'.
Tab to Retry, press Enter.
Within one second, check document.activeElement (body) and press Tab: focus jumps to the region after the demo.
Repeat on /patterns/activity-dashboard and /patterns/resource-detail.

evidence.method: Playwright: focus Retry, Enter, wait 150 ms, read activeElement, then Tab or Shift+Tab
evidence.observation: focusDuringLoading 'BODY' on all three pages; Tab → 'div "What each demo scenario render…" in main'; Shift+Tab → 'button "Reset demo"' (detail: 'a "Directory"').
focusImmediately body; after ~3 s focus on h3 'System directory' with visible outline.

issues.bestPracticeRationale: Focus loss is transient and is repaired automatically when loading ends, and the sequence a user reaches is still logical, so this is not recorded as a 2.4.3 failure. It still removes the focus indicator during the wait and can send a quick Tab past the demo; screen-reader effects of the body focus are untested (BLK-001).

sources.title: ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) Pattern
sources.relevantGuidance: If the invoking element no longer exists, focus is set on another element that provides logical work flow.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.3 Focus Order
sources.relevantGuidance: Order must preserve meaning and operability; used to justify the best-practice classification.

sourceRequirements.requirement: Move focus to a logical element when the focused control is removed.

engineeringJudgment: The demo headings already have tabIndex=-1 and a focus-visible style, so focusing them on Retry (instead of only after success) is the minimal change and keeps the existing success behaviour.
Alternative: keep the Alert mounted with Retry in a loading state (Button loading uses aria-disabled to keep focus); this changes the visual design, so it needs product agreement.
issues.likelyRootCause: retry() sets the request state to pending; the error branch (and its Retry button) unmounts immediately, and the focus effect only runs on state.status === 'success' (ResourceDirectory.tsx effect after useEffect load; ActivityDashboard.tsx:32; ResourceDetail Detail focusOnMount).
issues.proposedFix: In each demo's retry handler, focus the demo heading (headingRef) synchronously before calling load(), and keep the existing success-time focus as a no-op if already focused. For ResourceDetail, keep a stable heading element across pending/error/success (currently three different h3 elements share headingId) so a ref can be focused while pending.
issues.risksAndDependencies: Must stay consistent with A11Y-002 so the outcome status is still announced after focus moves. ResourceDetail renders different heading elements per state, which complicates the ref.
acceptanceCriteria: On all three pattern pages, 150 ms after pressing Enter on Retry, document.activeElement is the demo heading (or another visible in-demo element), not body.
After success, focus is on the demo heading with visible outline (unchanged behaviour).
Tab pressed during loading moves to the first focusable element after the heading inside the demo region, not beyond the demo.
manualVerification: Edge keyboard: each pattern page, scenario Error, Retry with Enter, immediately press Tab; focus stays inside the demo.
Confirm visible focus ring on the heading during loading at 1280x900 and 320x640.
issues.candidateAutomatedTest: Playwright e2e in e2e/patterns.spec.ts: select 'error', press Enter on Retry, expect(heading).toBeFocused() before the success state (use a short timeout). Vitest with fake timers on simulateRequest can assert toHaveFocus() during pending.

issues.title: Theme studio ramp chroma values are cut off with an ellipsis under WCAG text-spacing overrides

priority.rationale: Single tool page, single list; values are still in the DOM for AT, but sighted users who need increased spacing lose all 12 chroma values with no way to reveal them. Small CSS fix.

affectedUsers: Users with dyslexia or low vision who apply text-spacing user styles
Users with cognitive disabilities who increase letter and word spacing
issues.pattern: Static data list of color ramp steps (content, not a widget). See pattern matrix row P-17 'Theme studio'.
issues.observedBehavior: At 1280x900 with the 1.4.12 values injected (line-height 1.5, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em, paragraph spacing 2em), all 12 'C 0.0xx' chroma labels render as 'C 0.0…' / 'C 0.1…' (scrollWidth 63 > clientWidth 61) because .stripMeta sets overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap. The chroma value appears nowhere else on the page (occurrence count 1; export has no OKLCH values). Without overrides nothing is truncated; at 320 and 640 px the strip switches to four columns and does not truncate.
issues.expectedBehavior: With the 1.4.12 spacing applied, every ramp label is fully visible (wraps or the column grows), or a mechanism reveals the full value.
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155, viewport 1280x900, open http://localhost:5173/foundations/theme-studio.
Inject the CSS: * { line-height:1.5!important; letter-spacing:0.12em!important; word-spacing:0.16em!important } p { margin-bottom:2em!important } (bookmarklet or DevTools).
Scroll to the ramp strip under 'Ramp and roles'.
Observe the 'C' values end in an ellipsis; there is no hover/focus/expand way to read them.

evidence.method: Computed scrollWidth/clientWidth per label with and without spacing at 1280, 640 and 320
evidence.observation: 1280: 0/24 truncated; 1280-spacing: 12/24 truncated (all C values); 320, 320-spacing, 640-spacing: 0 truncated.
valueElsewhereCount 0; li text '50#f4f6ffL 97%C 0.012' (values exist in DOM).
Full 'C 0.012' labels.
'C 0.0…', 'C 0.1…' truncation.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing
sources.relevantGuidance: No loss of content or functionality when line height, paragraph, letter and word spacing are set to the listed values.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing
sources.relevantGuidance: 'Use of ellipses': text that is not truncated normally but is truncated when spaced, with no mechanism to show it, fails this criterion.

sourceRequirements.requirement: Spaced text must not be lost; ellipsis truncation is acceptable only with a reveal mechanism.

engineeringJudgment: Allowing the meta labels to wrap (remove nowrap/ellipsis, keep tabular numerals) is the least intrusive fix; the strip already reflows to four columns in narrow containers, so a container-query step to 6 columns at medium widths is an alternative.
issues.likelyRootCause: .stripMeta in ThemeStudio.module.css:443-449 combines overflow:hidden, text-overflow:ellipsis and white-space:nowrap inside a 12-column grid whose columns are only ~61px wide at 1280.
issues.proposedFix: Remove the ellipsis truncation from .stripMeta (allow wrapping with overflow-wrap:anywhere, or drop white-space:nowrap) or switch the strip to fewer columns when its container is narrow relative to the text (container query on the panel). Do not hide the value; do not rely on a title tooltip.
issues.risksAndDependencies: Visual change to the strip height in the studio; uses only existing tokens so lint:architecture style checks stay green.
acceptanceCriteria: With the 1.4.12 CSS injected at 1280x900, 640x450 and 320x640, 0 of 24 .stripMeta labels have scrollWidth > clientWidth and every label's full text is visible.
Without overrides the strip still renders all 12 steps without page-level horizontal scrolling at 320px.
manualVerification: Edge 1280x900: open /foundations/theme-studio, apply text-spacing bookmarklet, visually read all 'L' and 'C' values.
Repeat at 320x640 and in dark theme.
issues.candidateAutomatedTest: Playwright e2e (responsive.spec.ts): addStyleTag with the 1.4.12 CSS and assert every [class*=stripMeta] has scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1. Limits: only catches overflow-type truncation.

issues.title: Reason text for an unavailable RadioGroup option is dimmed to 2.5:1 contrast

priority.rationale: Shared composite (RadioGroup) so the dimming applies wherever an option is disabled with a description; currently one documented instance. Explanations for unavailable choices are information users need. Small CSS change.

locations.component: RadioGroup example data (disabled: true, description: 'Fully booked this week.')

issues.pattern: Unavailable option with explanation in a native radio group. See pattern matrix row P-05 'Radio group'.
issues.observedBehavior: The disabled option '17:00 to 20:00' and its description 'Fully booked this week.' are dimmed together with opacity 0.55. axe and computed values give 2.51:1 (light, #9c9fa5 on #f8f9fa, 14px) and 3.0:1 (dark, #5a5e64 on #0b0c0e) in all three products.
issues.expectedBehavior: The explanation of why the option is unavailable meets 4.5:1 so the reason can be read, while the disabled control itself may stay dimmed.
reproductionSteps: Start: Edge 155, 1280x900, open http://localhost:5173/components/radio-group.
Find 'Delivery window'; read 'Fully booked this week.' under the disabled '17:00 to 20:00' option.
Measure contrast (DevTools color picker or axe): 2.51:1 light, 3.0:1 dark.

evidence.observation: serious color-contrast on #_r_6_-evening-description, 2.51 and 3.

evidence.method: axe scoped to the element in all 6 product x theme combinations + computed opacity
evidence.observation: light 2.51, dark 3 in system-lab, harbor and meadow; opacity 0.55 on the option; radio disabled true.
Faint description under the disabled option.

issues.bestPracticeRationale: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component, and the description is associated with the disabled radio (aria-describedby) and dimmed with it, so this is not recorded as a conformance failure despite axe's 'serious' rating. The text is the only explanation of why the choice is unavailable, so low-vision users lose that information.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
sources.relevantGuidance: Incidental exception covers text that is part of an inactive user interface component.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
sources.relevantGuidance: 'Inactive User Interface Components' are not required to meet contrast requirements.

sources.title: ARIA APG Radio Group Pattern
sources.relevantGuidance: Radio group keyboard model (checked by native implementation).
sources.caveats: Implementation is native; APG consulted for the pattern contract only.

sourceRequirements.requirement: None normative (exempt). Best practice: keep explanatory text readable.

acceptanceCriteria: On /components/radio-group, the 'Fully booked this week.' description has contrast >= 4.5:1 in system-lab, harbor and meadow, light and dark (axe color-contrast shows no violation).
The disabled radio and its label remain visually dimmed and the radio stays disabled.
Cards appearance (if a disabled card option exists) keeps the same rule.

priority.rationale: Affects landmark/region navigation only; two instances; trivial fixes.

affectedUsers: Screen-reader users navigating by landmark or region

locations.component: Workbench usage section and code ScrollRegion
NarrowAndWide demo renders the same ScrollRegion twice

issues.pattern: Named region (section with aria-labelledby; ScrollRegion role=region). See pattern matrix row P-16 'Scrollable regions and data tables'.
issues.observedBehavior: Playwright ARIA snapshot of /playground shows 'region "Usage"' twice: the section is labelled by the Usage heading and the nested code ScrollRegion is labelled by the same heading (Playground.tsx:324 and :341). On /components/scroll-region the narrow and wide copies of the demo both expose 'region "Release history"'. axe best-practice rule landmark-unique flags both in every product/theme combination.
issues.expectedBehavior: Each region has a distinct name, for example 'Usage' and 'Usage code', and 'Release history (narrow container)' / '(wide container)'.
reproductionSteps: Open /playground?component=button in Edge.

landmark-unique n=1 on /playground and /components/scroll-region.

issues.bestPracticeRationale: Each region has a name and a role, so 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 are met; identical names make region navigation lists ambiguous. APG landmark guidance asks for unique labels when a role repeats.

sources.title: ARIA APG Landmark Regions
sources.relevantGuidance: If a page includes more than one landmark of the same role, each should have a unique label.
sources.caveats: region with a name is a landmark role.

sourceRequirements.requirement: Repeated landmark roles have unique labels.

issues.proposedFix: Give the Playground code ScrollRegion its own name (aria-label 'Usage code'). In NarrowAndWide (LayoutExamples.tsx), pass a width-specific suffix into the example's aria-label.
issues.risksAndDependencies: e2e/playground*.spec.ts may locate the snippet by region name; update selectors if so.

ARIA snapshot shows distinct names for every region on both pages.

issues.title: Products foundation skips from h2 to h4 in the 'Products × themes' specimens

priority.rationale: Single page, minor navigation friction; one-line fix.

affectedUsers: Screen-reader users navigating by heading level
issues.pattern: Document heading outline. See pattern matrix row P-02 'Page structure'.
issues.observedBehavior: Outline: H2 'Products × themes' followed directly by six H4 'Pending approvals' specimen headings (no H3). axe heading-order (best practice) flags it in light and dark.

issues.bestPracticeRationale: WCAG 2.2 does not require sequential heading levels; the headings exist and are programmatic (1.3.1 met). Skipped levels can suggest missing content to heading-level navigators.
